articles.title: Pitfall! - IGN
articles.summary: Would you believe that without David Crane, there would be no Mario?  No Sonic?  No Crash?  Thanks to one of Activision's earliest and greatest game makers, the Atari 2600 hosted the first real-deal side-scrolling platformer, and a genre was born.  The landmark title has now been successfully ported to your cellphone, thanks to the good ship JAMDAT.
articles.body:
MIDI sound effects Pitfall ! is still considered one of Activision's greatest triumphs. And for good reason, as the game has held up fantastically over the last two decades. Unless you are a true-blue graphics whore, it's impossible to not pick up the original Pitfall! and a be perfect content gamer for a good hour. JAMDAT has managed to successfully recreate the magic. This cellphone port contains the entire 2600 original--all 255 screens, every scorpion, every shimmering brick of gold. And it's still quite the challenge, however, some of that can be attributed to getting used to the keypad controls. Especially when it comes time to leap over those pesky crocodiles. Give it time, though, and you'll be falling through pits with the best of them. Forty minutes. That's all the time you have to master his jungle. There are exactly thirty-two treasures out there, waiting to be found. The more you find, the higher your point total. Points are subtracted, though, when you are hit by a rolling log. No such respite, though, if you are gobbled by a croc, fall in a tar pit, or are dumb enough to touch the campfire. And since that fire is a stationary object, you deserve to feel like a maroon for losing one of your precious three lives to it. The game is presented in a sort of quasi-letterbox since celly screens are not quite the same shape as your old television. The actual game happens along the top of the screen, while the bottom offers up a crib sheet for controls. It looks exactly like the old Atari game, just scaled down for the smaller-than-small screen. The sounds have also been faithfully recreated, including the unforgettable jungle bellow when you jump to a vine.

articles.title: Xbox Series X Review - IGN
articles.summary: Microsoft's mighty Tower of Power.
articles.body:
The Xbox Series X sneaks up on you. It’s a minimalist block with precisely one curve on the entire thing. And when you turn it on, the dashboard looks almost identical to the one that Xbox One gamers have been using for years. Even the power button makes the same beeps, and the packed-in controller is barely changed. It’s not until you fire up a game and are launched into smooth, native 4K amazingly quickly that the Series X justifies spending $500 to upgrade. This console makes few compromises and, now that Xbox Game Studios has launched a couple of technically amazing showcase games in Microsoft Flight Simulator and Forza Horizon 5 (both of which scored 10/10 on IGN), going back to even an Xbox One X would be agonizing.

From the moment you open the Xbox Series X box, it makes a great first impression with a presentation reminiscent of an Apple product. It’s clear that every aspect of that process has been carefully considered, including the console’s central, isolated placement in the box, making it feel like you’re opening a present. It’s befitting of a premium $500 device.

Xbox Series S and Series X Comparison Photos

That customer-first thinking continues with an easy initial setup when you plug the Series X in and turn it on. You can even use your smartphone to log into your account and toggle your settings and preferences while the box itself downloads and installs a firmware update. Once you’re up and running, you’ve got multiple options for bringing your existing library to the Series X – the best of which don’t require you to redownload anything. For instance, if your current Xbox is still hooked up to your network when you bring home the Series X, simply plug in the Series X and transfer all of your games right over the network – which, provided your network is up to snuff, is pretty quick. It’s as painless as upgrading a smartphone.

Let’s talk about the console design itself. It’s minimalist, yes, but bold. To my eye, it’s easily the best in Xbox history – when it’s standing vertically at least. On its side, it looks like a giant misplaced LEGO piece, and you can’t remove the vertical stand on the left side, which is awkward. But when stood tall, it’s big enough to confidently tower in your entertainment center while compact and subtle enough that it doesn’t dominate it.

The top of the Series X is something of an industrial designer’s magic trick; the concave ventilation screen gives an appealing look of both depth and premium quality when viewed at eye level or higher, and the green coloring on the inside half of those ventilation holes pops with a much-needed accent that makes the inside of the Series X appear to be illuminated even when it’s turned off.

On the front you have the power button, a single USB 3.2 port, a 4K Blu-ray drive with an eject button, and a controller pairing button. On the back, there’s an HDMI 2.1 out, two more USB ports, the power plug, an ethernet port, and the internal storage expansion slot. RIP, HDMI in and optical ports. I know those weren’t the Xbox One’s most popular features, but I’ll miss them, especially since it means I can no longer use my trusty old Astro A40 headphones.

I won’t miss fan noise, however, because there really isn’t any. Kudos to Microsoft’s engineers for making the Series X almost inaudibly quiet. Even playing games in 4K at 60 frames per second, this stoic ebony obelisk barely whispers. We measured just 40 decibels while playing Dirt 5 , which sounds great next to 60db for the same game on the One X. In the thermal department, the Series X also does very well. It’s a bit cooler than the Xbox One X, registering 42.5 degrees Celsius in Dirt 5 versus 56 degrees in the same game on the One X.

The Best Games to Play on Xbox Series X|S

If you’ve owned an Xbox One, navigating your new Series X will be instantly familiar. I do realize that’s anticlimactic for a lot of folks; until now, when we’ve bought an expensive new-generation console we’ve gotten a totally new experience. Microsoft has not done that here, opting instead for continuity across generations and sticking with an interface that, after eight years of tweaking, works pretty well. It may not be shiny or new but it is time-tested: it has every feature and third-party media app we’ve come to expect from a current console, with no obvious gaps or downgrades like we saw when the Xbox One first launched. On the Series X it’s snappier and more responsive, and a lot of functionality is easily accessed via a press of the Guide button on the controller. Some occasionally needed settings are still cumbersome to find, but at least there’s a system-level search functionality, similar to Windows and iPhone, that lets you search for things like “HDR setting.”

When it comes to power, this generation is no repeat of the previous one, which saw the Xbox One outgunned by Sony’s PlayStation 4 on both power and price. This time, the Xbox Series X’s main selling point is that it has 12.1 teraflops of computational power on tap for games to play with. It’s not a perfect measurement of speed, but on paper that’s twice as powerful as the Xbox One X and about 20% better than the PlayStation 5 – for the same $499 price that Sony’s charging.

In practice, that means 4K/60fps experiences are the new normal, and that boost in framerate is a very noticeable upgrade from the 4K/30fps treatments common on the Xbox One X and the upscaled or checkerboarded 4K/30 we usually see on the PS4 Pro . While the PS5 hasn't exactly struggled to keep up with third-party games over the past year, this generation is still only getting started, and the Series X has greater headroom for more ambitious games to grow into a few years down the line.

If you favor frame rate over all else, some games on the Series X offer a 120fps option , though doubling the frame rate usually comes at the cost of some amount of resolution. It’s also likely to cause some setup hassle, because not every 4K TV or HDMI cable supports 120Hz (thank you for including a 120Hz cable in the box, Microsoft). That said, the difference between 60Hz and 120Hz was nice but didn’t jump out at me the way the upgrade from 30 to 60 does, and I don’t generally think it’s worth sacrificing the resolution for. But your mileage may vary, and if you’re serious about competitive gaming, you might be glad the option is there.

The Series X’s superstar feature is its 1TB NVMe SSD drive. Games played from there, new and old alike, show tremendously impressive loading time improvements. Red Dead Redemption 2 , which takes 2:43 to go from Dashboard to playing on the Xbox One X, does so in just 1:05 on the Series X. Halo 5 improves from 1:07 to 0:25. Control went from 2:24 to 1:03. And State of Decay 2 took just 30 seconds on the Series X versus 1:06 on the One X. The SSD affects absolutely everything on this console in an utterly life-changing way. When you consider all the hours we’ve wasted staring at loading screens this past generation, this is arguably a bigger leap forward for console gaming than 4K.

What stings a little bit, though, is thinking about how quickly that 802GB of usable space will fill up when we start installing 136GB of Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War , 120GB of Halo: The Master Chief Collection , 72GB of Gears 5 , 72GB Cyberpunk 2077 , and so on. Especially when you’re looking at $220 for a 1TB expansion card that matches the SSD’s performance, those numbers are very scary. But again, Xbox One-generation games will run in their un-enhanced form from a regular USB 3.0 drive, so you can reserve all of the internal space for games that need it.

Speaking of speed, Quick Resume is the Series X’s other nearly omnipresent feature that I now wonder how I ever lived without. Being able to almost instantly pick up where you left off in any of your several most recently played games (provided that they're Series X-native) is an absolutely fantastic quality-of-life feature. It only takes about five to 10 seconds to go from selecting a game off of your list to actually playing exactly where you left off. There’s no need to go back through the splash screens, the main menu, or even load to a recent checkpoint. Much more than any previous console, the Series X makes me feel like it’s ready to be picked up and played at a moment’s notice, and that makes me want to use it more often. That said, the past year has shown us that Quick Resume isn't as reliable as it should be – for instance, if a game requires online authentication, like FIFA 22, Quick Resume almost always fails and you have to manually quit and restart it to play online.

A hidden cost savings of the Series X is that you can expect just about any Xbox One peripherals you own that aren’t named Kinect to seamlessly pair with the Series X. The new controllers are only slightly revised and older Xbox One controllers as well as the pricey Elites are still rock solid, so if you like your existing controller, you can bring it with you.

So far, the almost complete lack of any power-hungry next-gen-exclusive games to put those teraflops to a true test is the millstone around the Series X’s neck. Even with the aforementioned Forza Horizon 5 and Microsoft Flight Simulator, and Halo Infinite finally almost here, next to Sony's impressive output of first-party games Xbox still has a lot of catching up to do.

Happily, there’s no shortage of things to play thanks to full backward-compatibility out of the box. Just about everything from the Xbox One will work, and the substantial catalog of Xbox 360 games and handful from the original Xbox that were brought forward to the Xbox One carry over to the Series X, too. They also look and run better than they did on previous Xbox systems – such as enabling HDR on Halo 5 or a framerate approaching 60fps on Grand Theft Auto IV. It’s not unlike upgrading your PC. In some cases they benefit from Smart Delivery, Microsoft’s platform-level system that encourages developers to push you the best version of their game based on which Xbox it’s being played on. So if you buy Assassin’s Creed Valhalla for Xbox One now but then get a Series X as a gift in December, your progress will carry over seamlessly and your console will download any new tech or textures it needs in order to give you the optimized-for-Series-X-edition of Ubisoft’s new RPG. Compared to the PlayStation 5's sloppy handiling of some of its cross-generation upgrades, this past year has proven Smart Delivery to be very smart indeed.

articles.title: The Top 27 Best Batman Comics and Graphic Novels
articles.summary: In honor of Batman Day 2025, check out our updated list of the Caped Crusader's essential reads - these are the greatest Batman graphic novels and comics!
articles.body:
There's never been a better time to be a Batman fan. With multiple incarnations of the Dark Knight appearing in upcoming movies and TV series , and DC celebrating another Batman Day event, we figured now was the time to update our breakdown of the best Batman comics ever published. We've now expanded this list to include 27 stories, a significant number considering Batman originally debuted in the pages of 1939's Detective Comics #27.

A few criteria before we get started. This list of essentials is meant to focus on Batman comics that provide a complete, standalone reading experience rather than spotlighting individual issues or long comic runs. They don’t have to have originally been published in graphic novel form, but they do need to be available to read in a single collected edition now. We’re also limiting our focus to stories where Batman himself is the star of the show. Classics like Mad Love and Batgirl: Year One are must-read stories set in the world of Batman, but you won't find them on this list.

With that out of the way, here are the 27 best and most influential Batman graphic novels of all time. These are the comics that belong on any Bat-fan’s shelf. You can also check out our list of the top 10 best Batman crossovers and the 10 best Batman costumes of all time .

The 27 Greatest Batman Graphic Novels of All Time

If Batman: Year One were written today, it would be Batman: Earth One. It’s a modern retelling of Batman’s early years where he’s not an infallible master detective who moves like a shadow -- a point driven home when, while chasing a crook over the city rooftops, his grappling gun malfunctions and he lands in a pile of trash below. Also, instead of being best buds with Jim Gordon, he winds up socking him in the face.

The crucial element that makes this story work is the overhaul of Alfred Pennyworth’s character. No longer a kindly butler, Alfred is an ex-MI-6 agent who, instead of serving him tea and tending to his wounds, beats the crap out of Bruce to teach him a lesson. It’s a refreshing spin on the classic dynamic that lets us appreciate how Batman would adapt to a world with more realistic limitations.

To date, Earth One has spawned two sequels, and we're hopeful Johns and Frank have at least one more volume planned that will focus on a certain Clown Prince of Crime.

26. Flashpoint: Batman - Knight of Vengeance

Creators: Brian Azzarello & Eduardo Risso

Flashpoint marked a critical chapter in DC’s history, paving the way for the rebooted New 52 universe and everything else that followed. But as it turns out, the best part of this massive crossover didn’t involve The Flash himself, but rather Batman.

In this alternate timeline, Thomas Wayne became Batman after his son was murdered in front of him. The result is a vigilante who manages to top even Bruce Wayne in the brooding and scowling department. Knight of Vengeance showcases a darker, meaner Gotham City that plays perfectly to Brian Azzarello and Eduardo Risso’s storytelling strengths.

Though this book technically serves as a piece of a much larger crossover, it also reads perfectly well on its own. It also features one of the most haunting endings you’ll find in any Batman comic.

Creators: Brian Michael Bendis & Nick Derington

When Marvel Comics mainstay Brian Michael Bendis made the jump to DC in 2019, it was inevitable he'd write a Batman story. But anyone who expected Bendis to return to the type of gritty crime drama that defined his early comics career was probably shocked by the contents of Batman Universe. Sometimes surprises can be a great thing.

In a world where so many Batman storytellers seem intent on outdoing each other in terms of darkness and violence, it's refreshing to have a comic that celebrates the lighter side of the Caped Crusader. Universe is a zany romp that spans the full scope of the DCU and shares as much in common with the classic Silver Age comics as it does contemporary Batman fare. It's a book that also benefits mightily from the dynamic art of Doom Patrol artist Nick Derington.

A mad man is targeting Gotham's elite and next on his hit list is millionaire playboy Bruce Wayne. This is Batman's introduction to his most nefarious villain, the Joker. Where Alan Moore's The Killing Joke tells the origin of the Clown Prince of Crime, The Man Who Laughs details the first tussle between Joker and Batman.

Brubaker is one of the best crime writers in comics. He manages to bring some of that noir flair to The Man Who Laughs while maintaining the proper tone and pace for a good Batman yarn. To my knowledge this is the only story to ever suggest that, like Bruce Wayne, the Joker had to practice to perfect his art. And that's ultimately what makes the Joker so frightening. His psychosis is not chaotic, not as random as you might think. There's a methodology and a purposefulness to many of his actions.

Creators: Denny O’Neil & Trevor Von Eden

Venom opens with one of the biggest failures in Batman's career. A little girl is trapped. Drowning. And Batman isn't strong enough to save her. Distraught, the Dark Knight finds a new alternative to strength training -- a little pill that triples his strength. Of course, it's highly addictive and the always-in-control hero loses his grip, nearly assassinating Jim Gordon just to get his fix. It's a look at a side of Batman we rarely see.

Venom is one of those stories that is a struggle to rank. The premise is stronger than the actual writing. Batman fights a shark. So, there's that. But there are moments, strong moments, where O'Neil tests the limits of Batman's commitment to his crusade. And it's enough to make Venom one of the more memorable Batman stories ever told.

Creators: Marv Wolfman, George Perez, Jim Aparo & Tom Grummett

Dick Grayson and Jason Todd became Robin out of circumstance. They didn't really choose the role, it was chosen for them. Tim Drake is different. He takes an active role in becoming the third Robin. A Lonely Place of Dying isn't just an origin tale of Robin #3, it's the best response to the question: "Why does Batman need Robin?"

The answer, it turns out, isn't to keep Batman from the dark side or as some subconscious way of restoring Bruce Wayne's lost youth. When Batman has to consider the safety of a young sidekick, he's more likely to think things through. He'll take more precautions. He'll be safer. Robin, just by virtue of being at his side, keeps Batman alive a little longer. Now, if that doesn't make you want to read the only worthwhile Robin origin, you just don't like Batman stories.

A year into his crime-fighting career, Batman has only faced mobsters, thugs, and a few crazies. Monster Men is Batman's first encounter with anything super-human. Hugo Strange is creating monstrous creatures, stronger than the Dark Knight and with a mindless thirst for blood. Now, Batman must adapt to a new kind of villain. This is the moment where Batman goes from street legend onto the path of superhero.

The best Batman books push the Caped Crusader to his limits. This story is about Bruce Wayne learning he has limits.

Batman/Elmer Fudd Special #1 is the quintessential example of a comic with no business being as great as it is. One of several crossovers between DC characters and the Loony Tunes cast published in 2017, this comic introduces a bizarrely grounded version of Elmer who blames Bruce Wayne for the murder of the woman he loves. Naturally, a Batman/Elmer Fudd team-up ensues.

This comic isn't blind to the inherent absurdity of its premise, but it also treats that premise with a surprising level of gravitas and weight. It doesn't hurt that writer Tom King and artist Lee Weeks prove every bit the creative Dynamic Duo here that they are on King's main Batman run. There's a reason this issue is one of the few comics to earn a 10 rating from IGN .

Creators: Jim Starlin & Bernie Wrightson

While it doesn’t feature Bane as the villain, Batman: The Cult is easily one of the heaviest influences on The Dark Knight Rises. Let’s just say that the Nolan brothers know a good Batman comic when they see one.

The Cult showcases Batman at his most psychologically vulnerable. In this story he’s captured by Deacon Blackfire and his cultists and subjected to torture and brainwashing. The result is an unnerving and even psychedelic Batman tale that uses Bernie Wrightson’s gorgeous art to convey the instability of Batman’s unraveling mind.

The Cult has proven to be a divisive story, in large part because it doesn’t portray Batman as the tough, capable hero he normally is. But his failures in The Cult only make his eventual victory that much more satisfying.

Scott Snyder and Greg Capullo had a tall order to fill when they took the reins of DC’s relaunched Batman comic in 2011. They had to assuage the fears of those fans nervous about DC’s New 52 reboot and somehow follow the impossible act that is writer Grant Morrison. And somehow they succeeded in both goals.

Snyder and Capullo kicked off their run by introducing a brand new group of villains to Gotham City - the Court of Owls. This centuries-old, shadowy organization forced Batman to confront the fact that he doesn’t know his own city nearly as well as he thought. That fueled a personal odyssey that dragged Batman through the depths of Gotham and pitted him against a new archrival from a very unexpected source.

“The Court of Owls” immediately established Batman as one of the best comics of the New 52 era and Snyder and Capullo as one of the most effective teams working in comics.

Creators: Steve Englehart, Len Wein, Marshall Rogers & Walt Simonson

If you haven't read Strange Apparitions, chances are you've never heard of Bruce Wayne's best love interest, Silver St. Cloud. She's smart enough to deduce Batman's true identity and strong enough to break the Batman's heart. And that's just part of the mix in this great tale from the late '70s featuring underappreciated lunatic Hugo Strange (back from the dead) and the Joker (creating more dead). Plus, as a bonus, you get to see Hugo Strange dressed as Batman.

Batman: Year One gets a little too much credit for "reinventing Batman." The truth is that there were great Batman stories before Year One. This is the best you'll find from the pre-Year One era that's been collected in a TPB. And it serves as a worthwhile introduction to Hugo Strange.

Where did Bruce Wayne go to school? We know about Wayne's training to become the Batman, but in Gothic, we get a glimpse into Bruce Wayne's life before his parents were murdered. This ties into a series of grisly murders in Batman's early days in the cape and cowl.

Gothic is a detective story, a horror story, and a thriller that teams Morrison with the great Klaus Janson. Religion and Batman aren't married in comics as often as they should be. Morrison plays it perfectly. For those a little worried about a "Morrison head-trip," relax. Nothing in these pages will damage your brain… too much.

Knightfall is an example of a story that overcomes the shortcomings of its art and writing, which were flawed if only because of several change-ups over its publication. The story is so essential to Batman’s character that it was the main inspiration for The Dark Knight Rises movie, further expanding its popularity and cementing it as a classic.

In Knightfall, Bane breaks out all of Arkham Asylum’s criminals to exhaust Batman. Once the Caped Crusader is exhausted physically and mentally, Bane breaks his back over his knee. Ouch. What follows next is why the story made this list. Batman hands over the mantle to Jean-Paul Valley, aka Azreal, who soon loses his mind and starts killing criminals. Batman must train and rebuild himself from the ground up with help from Lady Shiva, and then he returns to Gotham to reclaim his mantle from Azreal.

The story shows why Bruce Wayne’s morality makes him the ideal Batman. He is uniquely suited to be the kind of hero that Gotham needs, which is made plain by juxtaposing him with the murderous Azreal.

14. Batman: The War of Jokes and Riddles

Creators: Tom King, Mikel Janin & Clay Mann

Plenty of Batman comics have flashed back to the early days of Bruce Wayne’s costumed career, but few have done it as successfully as “The War of Jokes and Riddles.”

In this extended flashback saga, writer Tom King and artists Mikel Janin and Clay Mann explore a Batman just young and naïve enough to think he’s on the verge of cleaning up Gotham City for good. A devastating gang war between Joker and Riddler shows him just how wrong he is. This story stands out both because it pushes Batman to the psychological brink and because it showcases so many iconic villains. And somehow, D-List baddie Kite-Man outshines them all.

While “The War of Jokes and Riddles” has its place as part of King’s larger, 100-issue Batman run, it also stands alone as a compelling glimpse into one of the most formative periods in Batman’s war on crime.

Two stories solidified the notion that Batman can kick anyone's ass. The first was Frank Miller's The Dark Knight Returns, where Batman outwits and outduels Superman, the other is Mark Waid's excellent JLA story, Tower of Babel.

Batman, we discover, has a plan for everything. That includes what to do if any of his allies in the Justice League go rogue. He's prepared to take down any of his friends when necessary. And when an enemy unlocks those secret plans and uses them against the JLA, we get to see Batman's obsessive planning come to fruition.

Set in the Victorian era, the origin of Batman hasn't changed much in Gotham By Gaslight. Bruce Wayne's parents were murdered, he travelled abroad to train so that he could return to Gotham as its protector. Only catch is that while Bruce was in London, a madman was on the loose cutting up prostitutes. And when Bruce returns home to Gotham, the murders follow him. If you're going to suspect someone of slashing up ladies with a scalpel, why not the eccentric son of a doctor? After all, can Bruce Wayne explain his nocturnal habits?

Gotham By Gaslight is a tightly woven mystery that never tries to do too much. Sometimes Elseworlds tales throw in every bit of Batman lore and the Cray computers to boot. Wisely, Augustyn sticks to what makes sense for the story and pulls off one of the better tales in Batman's long history.

Jeph Loeb has mastered the lengthy storyline that cycles through Batman's Rogues Gallery. Usually these are stories from Batman's past, but Hush is a modern tale that uses some of the same clever gimmicks as The Long Halloween. We're left to wonder at the identity of a new mastermind villain named Hush who's playing all of Batman's old enemies in an effort to ruin the Dark Knight's life. It's a mystery with a controversial resolution, but if the journey is what matters, well, then Hush belongs on the list of the 25 must-read Batman books.

While we’re not a big fan of how Hush resolves itself, the individual pieces are brilliant. This is one of the few pre-DC Rebirth Batman stories to give some notable page space to explore the Batman/Catwoman relationship in depth, which makes it noteworthy by itself. The real star, though, is Jim Lee's art, which just might be his best work in his time at DC Comics.

10. Batman: Whatever Happened to the Caped Crusader?

Batman: Whatever Happened to the Caped Crusader? came along during a period where Bruce Wayne was believed to be dead, but it isn’t actually tied to regular Batman continuity. This story serves as more a hypothetical “What if?” scenario, as Batman’s closest allies and most bitter enemies come together to pay tribute at his wake.

Basically, this story is intended as a thematic companion piece to 1986’s Superman: Whatever Happened to the Man of Tomorrow? And while it’s tough to rival a creative team as good as Alan Moore and Curt Swan, Neil Gaiman and Andy Kubert are as talented a duo as you’ll find at DC. Together, they weave a whimsical and wistful tribute to a pop culture icon.

Creators: Scott Snyder, Jock & Francesco Francavilla

The Black Mirror tells two distinct stories drawn by two different artists -- both masters in their own right -- and then marries them together in the end with an unexpected (and polarizing) twist.

Most notable -- and potentially blasphemous -- is that this story stars Dick Grayson under the cowl instead of Bruce Wayne. Commissioner Gordon isn’t happy with it, but over the course of the story they form a bond not unlike the one with Bruce in Batman: Year One.

But the true obstacle for this new Batman comes in the form of James Gordon Jr., the Commissioner’s psychotic murderer of a son and modern day classic villain. Thanks to him, the tale is steeped in horror and full of deftly executed twists, not to mention the mystery he is responsible for is one that even Bruce would have had trouble with.

The name says it all. This is Batman, set a hundred years after the original's Gotham debut. Sadly, Gotham City is no better than it was a century ago. The police are still ravaged by corruption and too much of the city is gripped by poverty. But there is hope. There is a Batman. At least, that's the myth. No, this isn't Bruce Wayne at 120 years old. This is a new man in the suit, with a new Robin. But as we learn, the cape and cowl have become part of a legacy. A legacy most of Gotham has forgotten. Well, they're about to get a reminder.

Year 100 is different. Not just because it's set in the future. This is the rare Batman story that doesn't try to hang tight to the Bruce Wayne version of Batman. It's fresh and new and exciting. And yet, it has some very clear connections to Batman: Year One, keeping this wild fantasy of a futuristic Dark Knight tethered to the core mythology.

A scourge of the undead has hit Gotham City, turning its lowliest citizens into vampire warriors. The only thing keeping the vamps from turning Gotham into a buffet is Batman. One problem -- he's been infected too. Batman has often been called a creature of the night. In Red Rain, that's literal. Batman's challenge is two-fold: Stop the vamps from taking over the city and resist the urge to break his "one rule" and feed on another human being.

Long before True Blood, the vampire craze hit comics thanks to the almost abstract art of Kelley Jones and the heavy inks of Malcolm Jones III. Batman's ears never stood so tall before. In another artist's hands, Red Rain might read like a farce. But this is an example of the perfect marriage between story and art.

When Batman and his nemesis Ra's al Ghul find themselves chasing the same assassin, the two form an unexpected partnership. One that reunites Batman with Talia al Ghul, one of his stronger love interests. Is Batman ready to have a father-in-law like Ra's al Ghul? To become a father himself? The answer may surprise you.

People love the Joker and claim he is the perfect foil for the Batman. However, Ra's al Ghul can be the best Batman villain if the proper writer gets a hold of him. That's what you get with Son of the Demon, the perfect Ra's al Ghul tale. It's a brilliant, perfectly paced story that also happens to be the origin for one of the newest (and most interesting) Robins. For years, this book was impossible to find, but thanks to the introduction of Batman's son, Damian Wayne, Son of the Demon has been reprinted and is now readily available.

5. Arkham Asylum: A Serious House on Serious Earth

Arkham Asylum is home to some of the most twisted villains the DCU has to offer. What is it like to walk its winding halls and be confronted by by so many deranged killers and madmen? Arkham Asylum: A Serious House on Serious Earth is as close as we ever want to get to experiencing that for ourselves.

This 1989 graphic novel follows Batman’s surreal journey as he ventures inside an Arkham overrun by rioting inmates. Even as he encounters one iconic foe after another, he learns about the twisted history of the facility and the possibly supernatural forces at play. With a creative team as unique as Grant Morrison and Dave McKean, this is an odyssey neither Batman noir his readers will soon forget.

Someone in Gotham's decided to make a killing during the holidays. Each issue tackles another holiday as the year winds round. This new holiday killer has the mob, the cops, Arkham's crazies and the Batman all on edge. The Long Halloween is both a great mystery, among the best told in Batman's long history, and a new look at the Dark Knight's early career, when the status quo of Gotham City was changing.

The Long Halloween has all the ingredients of a classic Batman story: A mysterious killer, appearances by notable villains, striking visuals, and an imperfect ending to the case. Special credit to Loeb for making one of the dumbest characters ever created, Calendar Man, appear interesting and necessary. As an added bonus, Jeph Loeb and Tim Sale reunited for a worthy sequel series, Dark Victory.

The Joker. Batman's greatest foe. His goal is chaos, but the beauty of his madness is the incredible amount of thought he puts into each caper. In the Killing Joke, the Clown Prince of Crime decides he wants to prove that, given the right push, anyone would fall into madness. To go about this, he torments down-to-earth Jim Gordon. All the while, we're given glimpses into the Joker's origin and see what pushed him over the edge.

The Killing Joke isn't just a brilliant origin story for comics' most famed villain, it also clearly defines what separates the good guys from the crazy guys. When push comes to shove, the sane ones shove back; the crazies allow themselves to go over the edge.

Creators: Frank Miller & David Mazzucchelli

Who would dress up like a bat and prance around the city fighting crime? We all know that answer. Who would stand by his side? That's the story we learn in Year One. Batman and Gordon arrive in Gotham around the same time, both carrying a lot of baggage. Though they spend the year making their fair share of mistakes, they form an uneasy partnership, one that will last throughout their careers.

Whenever a new Batman movie is announced, the first question is always: "Who's the villain?" And yet, the best Batman story of all time remains the one that features no marquee villains. At best, you get a cameo from Selina Kyle. Otherwise, this is a story about two men trying to do right in a city where everything has gone wrong. Perhaps that's what makes it so strong. There's no reliance on campy villains or a threat that would wipe out all of Gotham. This is street crime and corruption. This is the impossible battle, the one Batman and Jim Gordon can never win.

This is the one where Batman kicks Superman's ass. Set a decade after Batman's retirement, The Dark Knight Returns offers a grim vision of the future of Gotham City. Times are bleak and Gotham is in need of a hero. And Bruce Wayne? Well, he's been fighting his obsession for a decade. He simply can't hold out any longer. He puts the suit back on to face off against his oldest foe and his oldest friend.

The Dark Knight Returns is a masterpiece of comic-book storytelling. The pages are packed, sometimes with dozens of panels. Overcrowded, even. And yet, Miller creates a distinct pacing through each page and builds to perhaps the most optimistic ending in any Batman story. Yeah, Frank Miller ends with a touch of optimism.

For being just as entertaining the first time we read it as the last, creating the definitive dark and moody characterization of the Caped Crusader that is still channeled to this day, and for answering the age old question of "Who would win, Batman or Superman?", The Dark Knight Returns is the greatest Batman graphic novel of all time.

What are your favorite tales of The Batman? Let's discuss in the comments below! And be sure to check out IGN's picks for the 25 best Spider-Man comics too.

We've now expanded this list to include 27 stories, a significant number considering Batman originally debuted in the pages of 1939's Detective Comics #27.

A few criteria before we get started. This list of essentials is meant to focus on Batman comics that provide a complete, standalone reading experience rather than spotlighting individual issues or long comic runs. They don’t have to have originally been published in graphic novel form, but they do need to be available to read in a single collected edition now. We’re also limiting our focus to stories where Batman himself is the star of the show. Classics like Mad Love and Batgirl: Year One are must-read stories set in the world of Batman, but you won't find them on this list.

With that out of the way, here are the 27 best and most influential Batman graphic novels of all time. These are the comics that belong on any Bat-fan’s shelf. You can also check out our list of the top 10 best Batman crossovers and the 10 best Batman costumes of all time .
The 27 Greatest Batman Graphic Novels of All Time

If Batman: Year One were written today, it would be Batman: Earth One. It’s a modern retelling of Batman’s early years where he’s not an infallible master detective who moves like a shadow -- a point driven home when, while chasing a crook over the city rooftops, his grappling gun malfunctions and he lands in a pile of trash below. Also, instead of being best buds with Jim Gordon, he winds up socking him in the face.

The crucial element that makes this story work is the overhaul of Alfred Pennyworth’s character. No longer a kindly butler, Alfred is an ex-MI-6 agent who, instead of serving him tea and tending to his wounds, beats the crap out of Bruce to teach him a lesson. It’s a refreshing spin on the classic dynamic that lets us appreciate how Batman would adapt to a world with more realistic limitations.
To date, Earth One has spawned two sequels, and we're hopeful Johns and Frank have at least one more volume planned that will focus on a certain Clown Prince of Crime.

The real star, though, is Jim Lee's art, which just might be his best work in his time at DC Comics.
10. Batman: Whatever Happened to the Caped Crusader?

Batman: Whatever Happened to the Caped Crusader? came along during a period where Bruce Wayne was believed to be dead, but it isn’t actually tied to regular Batman continuity. This story serves as more a hypothetical “What if?” scenario, as Batman’s closest allies and most bitter enemies come together to pay tribute at his wake.

Basically, this story is intended as a thematic companion piece to 1986’s Superman: Whatever Happened to the Man of Tomorrow? And while it’s tough to rival a creative team as good as Alan Moore and Curt Swan, Neil Gaiman and Andy Kubert are as talented a duo as you’ll find at DC. Together, they weave a whimsical and wistful tribute to a pop culture icon.
Creators: Scott Snyder, Jock & Francesco Francavilla
The Black Mirror tells two distinct stories drawn by two different artists -- both masters in their own right -- and then marries them together in the end with an unexpected (and polarizing) twist.

Most notable -- and potentially blasphemous -- is that this story stars Dick Grayson under the cowl instead of Bruce Wayne. Commissioner Gordon isn’t happy with it, but over the course of the story they form a bond not unlike the one with Bruce in Batman: Year One.

But the true obstacle for this new Batman comes in the form of James Gordon Jr., the Commissioner’s psychotic murderer of a son and modern day classic villain. Thanks to him, the tale is steeped in horror and full of deftly executed twists, not to mention the mystery he is responsible for is one that even Bruce would have had trouble with.

The name says it all. This is Batman, set a hundred years after the original's Gotham debut. Sadly, Gotham City is no better than it was a century ago. The police are still ravaged by corruption and too much of the city is gripped by poverty. But there is hope. There is a Batman. At least, that's the myth. No, this isn't Bruce Wayne at 120 years old. This is a new man in the suit, with a new Robin. But as we learn, the cape and cowl have become part of a legacy. A legacy most of Gotham has forgotten. Well, they're about to get a reminder.

Year 100 is different. Not just because it's set in the future. This is the rare Batman story that doesn't try to hang tight to the Bruce Wayne version of Batman. It's fresh and new and exciting. And yet, it has some very clear connections to Batman: Year One, keeping this wild fantasy of a futuristic Dark Knight tethered to the core mythology.

A scourge of the undead has hit Gotham City, turning its lowliest citizens into vampire warriors. The only thing keeping the vamps from turning Gotham into a buffet is Batman. One problem -- he's been infected too. Batman has often been called a creature of the night. In Red Rain, that's literal. Batman's challenge is two-fold: Stop the vamps from taking over the city and resist the urge to break his "one rule" and feed on another human being.

Long before True Blood, the vampire craze hit comics thanks to the almost abstract art of Kelley Jones and the heavy inks of Malcolm Jones III. Batman's ears never stood so tall before. In another artist's hands, Red Rain might read like a farce. But this is an example of the perfect marriage between story and art.

When Batman and his nemesis Ra's al Ghul find themselves chasing the same assassin, the two form an unexpected partnership. One that reunites Batman with Talia al Ghul, one of his stronger love interests. Is Batman ready to have a father-in-law like Ra's al Ghul? To become a father himself? The answer may surprise you.

People love the Joker and claim he is the perfect foil for the Batman. However, Ra's al Ghul can be the best Batman villain if the proper writer gets a hold of him. That's what you get with Son of the Demon, the perfect Ra's al Ghul tale. It's a brilliant, perfectly paced story that also happens to be the origin for one of the newest (and most interesting) Robins. For years, this book was impossible to find, but thanks to the introduction of Batman's son, Damian Wayne, Son of the Demon has been reprinted and is now readily available.
5. Arkham Asylum: A Serious House on Serious Earth

Arkham Asylum is home to some of the most twisted villains the DCU has to offer. What is it like to walk its winding halls and be confronted by by so many deranged killers and madmen? Arkham Asylum: A Serious House on Serious Earth is as close as we ever want to get to experiencing that for ourselves.

This 1989 graphic novel follows Batman’s surreal journey as he ventures inside an Arkham overrun by rioting inmates. Even as he encounters one iconic foe after another, he learns about the twisted history of the facility and the possibly supernatural forces at play. With a creative team as unique as Grant Morrison and Dave McKean, this is an odyssey neither Batman noir his readers will soon forget.

Someone in Gotham's decided to make a killing during the holidays. Each issue tackles another holiday as the year winds round. This new holiday killer has the mob, the cops, Arkham's crazies and the Batman all on edge. The Long Halloween is both a great mystery, among the best told in Batman's long history, and a new look at the Dark Knight's early career, when the status quo of Gotham City was changing.

The Long Halloween has all the ingredients of a classic Batman story: A mysterious killer, appearances by notable villains, striking visuals, and an imperfect ending to the case. Special credit to Loeb for making one of the dumbest characters ever created, Calendar Man, appear interesting and necessary. As an added bonus, Jeph Loeb and Tim Sale reunited for a worthy sequel series, Dark Victory.

The Joker. Batman's greatest foe. His goal is chaos, but the beauty of his madness is the incredible amount of thought he puts into each caper. In the Killing Joke, the Clown Prince of Crime decides he wants to prove that, given the right push, anyone would fall into madness. To go about this, he torments down-to-earth Jim Gordon. All the while, we're given glimpses into the Joker's origin and see what pushed him over the edge.

The Killing Joke isn't just a brilliant origin story for comics' most famed villain, it also clearly defines what separates the good guys from the crazy guys. When push comes to shove, the sane ones shove back; the crazies allow themselves to go over the edge.
Creators: Frank Miller & David Mazzucchelli

Who would dress up like a bat and prance around the city fighting crime? We all know that answer. Who would stand by his side? That's the story we learn in Year One. Batman and Gordon arrive in Gotham around the same time, both carrying a lot of baggage. Though they spend the year making their fair share of mistakes, they form an uneasy partnership, one that will last throughout their careers.

Whenever a new Batman movie is announced, the first question is always: "Who's the villain?" And yet, the best Batman story of all time remains the one that features no marquee villains. At best, you get a cameo from Selina Kyle. Otherwise, this is a story about two men trying to do right in a city where everything has gone wrong. Perhaps that's what makes it so strong. There's no reliance on campy villains or a threat that would wipe out all of Gotham. This is street crime and corruption. This is the impossible battle, the one Batman and Jim Gordon can never win.

This is the one where Batman kicks Superman's ass. Set a decade after Batman's retirement, The Dark Knight Returns offers a grim vision of the future of Gotham City. Times are bleak and Gotham is in need of a hero. And Bruce Wayne? Well, he's been fighting his obsession for a decade. He simply can't hold out any longer. He puts the suit back on to face off against his oldest foe and his oldest friend.

The Dark Knight Returns is a masterpiece of comic-book storytelling. The pages are packed, sometimes with dozens of panels. Overcrowded, even. And yet, Miller creates a distinct pacing through each page and builds to perhaps the most optimistic ending in any Batman story. Yeah, Frank Miller ends with a touch of optimism.

For being just as entertaining the first time we read it as the last, creating the definitive dark and moody characterization of the Caped Crusader that is still channeled to this day, and for answering the age old question of "Who would win, Batman or Superman?", The Dark Knight Returns is the greatest Batman graphic novel of all time.
What are your favorite tales of The Batman? Let's discuss in the comments below! And be sure to check out IGN's picks for the 25 best Spider-Man comics too.

articles.title: VALORANT Champions: Paper Rex, primer finalista tras vencer a Evil Geniuses en un partido ajustado
articles.standfirst: Los de APAC remontaron en Bind y Pearl un encuentro que comenzaron perdiendo en Ascent
articles.summary: Paper Rex y Evil Geniuses se jugaban el todo por el todo en la semifinal. El equipo de APAC quería dar otra sorpresa más y ganarse un hueco en la gran final del sábado. Los genios
articles.body: Paper Rex y Evil Geniuses se jugaban el todo por el todo en la semifinal. El equipo de APAC quería dar otra sorpresa más y ganarse un hueco en la gran final del sábado. Los genios querían llevarse otra alegría en frente de su público, superando a los tailandeses y demostrando el gran nivel de la liga americana. Han protagonizado un encuentro espectacular, en el que empezó ganando Evil Geniuses en Ascent, tras remontar la ventaja de los de APAC, pero que se igualaba en Bind con la remontada de los asiáticos. Finalmente, en Pearl, el overtime ha caído del lado de los asiáticos, que cerraban con un 14-12. Crónica Evil Geniuses-Paper Rex El primer mapa fue Ascent, y comenzó con Paper Rex por delante, superando claramente a EG. Se llevaron las dos primeras rondas, pero los estadounidenses respondieron en la bonus. Sin embargo, no eran capaces de parar a los de APAC, y se les hacía difícil, llegando al 1-4 en contra. Sin embargo, finalmente leyeron la estrategia de Paper Rex, cerrando el primer bando con un 5-7 que les permitía soñar. El cambio de bando pareció favorecer a Evil Geniuses. Con una buena respuesta a la defensa de Paper Rex, alcanzaron el 7-7. Sin embargo los asiáticos sacaron de nuevo ventaja hasta el 8-10, y cuando parecía que iban a llegar a la undécima, C0M se inventó un clutch increíble que puso el 9-10. Finalmente, los genios consiguieron remontar, y con cuatro rondas de máximo nivel alcanzaron el 13-10. El segundo mapa fue Bind, y Evil Geniuses aprovechó su inicio en defensa, y comenzó superando claramente a los de APAC, con un 3-1. Posteriormente aumentaron su ventaja, pero finalmente el encuentro terminó con un resultado de 7-5 en la primera mitad. Los de APAC se habían acercado, pero en defensa no fueron capaces de terminar de recuperarse. Evil Geniuses volvió a poner tierra de por medio, y el resultado se situaba 9-5 para ellos. Sin embargo, Shomething estaba buscando dar una sorpresa, y lo demostró haciendo lo imposible con Reina, y llevó el encuentro al 9-9. Un 3k de D4v4i facilitaba los dobles dígitos, y Paper Rex se acercaba a la victoria en el segundo mapa. Something ponía el punto de partido, y finalmente un 3k de Jinggg ponía lel 9-13 y el 1-1 en la eliminatoria. Pearl fue el tercer y definitivo mapa, y en él Evil Geniuses empezaba dominando 3-0 desde el lado defensor. Sin embargo, Paper Rex se recuperó, y un 3k de Mindfreak llevó el encuentro al 3-4. Finalmente alcanzaron el 3-6, pero los americanos pusieron las tablas al cambio de bando. Tras este, sin embargo, Evil Geniuses se mantuvo imparable, consiguiendo las cuatro primeras rondas del ataque y poniendo contra las cuerdas a los de APAC. Del 6-6 pasaron al 11-6, pero de nuevo volvió a activarse Paper Rex. Su ataque mejoró, y llevaron el encuentro a la máxima igualdad, poniéndolo 11-11. Justo cuando parecía que Evil Geniuses tenía el partido en su mano, tras plantar y en un tres contra uno contra F0rsaken, el jugador asiático lo llevaba al overtime con un 3k con la odin. Mindfreak conseguía el primer punto del tiempo extra, pero EG respondía. Finalmente en el segundo overtime, Something se engargaba de poner el 12-14 y dar la victoria a Paper Rex.

articles.title: VALORANT Champions: Fnatic no puede con LOUD y cae con la cabeza alta
articles.standfirst: Los ingleses buscaron la remontada, pero no consiguieron completarla
articles.summary: El partido de semifinales del lower bracket era una oportunidad para los fans del VALORANT mundial de ver la que podría haber sido la final. LOUD y Fnatic se veían las caras de nue
articles.body: El partido de semifinales del lower bracket era una oportunidad para los fans del VALORANT mundial de ver la que podría haber sido la final. LOUD y Fnatic se veían las caras de nuevo, en un encuentro que de ganar los brasileños sería su revancha por la final del Lock In. Finalmente así ha sido. Tras más de tres horas de partido, LOUD ha eliminado a Fnatic con tres mapas que han hecho vibrar el KIA Forum de Los Ángeles. El primero, Split, ha sido claramente de LOUD, pero posteriormente los ingleses se han rehecho, para caer en el Haven final. Crónica Fnatic-LOUD Fnatic y LOUD comenzaron las hostilidades en Split. Empezaron muy igualados, con los brasileños consiguiendo una ventaja de 3-0. Fnatic intentaba responder, pero no tardaron en sacar más ventaja los de la VCT americana. Al cambio de bando el resultado era claro, un 8-4. Y no pudo hacer mucho más Fnatic en el segundo tramo. No sacaron ninguna ronda, ya que Saadhak y compañía se mostraron muy fuertes en defensa. Finalmente el resultado fue de 13-4, que dejaba a los ingleses en un muy mal lugar. El segundo mapa fue Ascent. En él LOUD volvió a sacar ventaja, pero Fnatic despertó, poniendo el 3-3. La igualdad era máxima, y aunque el conjunto brasileño alcanzó el 4-7, al cambio de bando un 3k de Derke puso el 5-7. Fnatic empezó la segunda parte haciéndose con su primera ronda de pistolas de este enfrentamiento. Se recuperaron hasta el 7-7 y sacaron ventaja llegando a situarse 9-7. Sin embargo, LOUD igualó a nueve, pero Fnatic supo imponerse, mostrando casta de campeón. Haven fue el mapa decisivo. LOUD sacaba ventaja, pero Fnatic recortaba. A pesar de que los brasileños llegaron a situarse 4-1, el conjunto europeo se recuperó, y con rondas muy ajustadas alcanzó el 4-4. Sin embargo, el equipo de Aspas sacó ventaja finalmente en la defensa, llevándose las últimas cuatro rondas, y cerrando la media parte 4-8. Tras el cambio de bando sacaron las dos primeras rondas, pero no fueron capaces de recuperarse completamente. LOUD volvió a la carga, y terminó cerrando el mapa y la eliminatoria con un resultado de 7-13.

articles.title: Boaster: "La temporada es muy larga, los jugadores necesitamos más tiempo de descanso"
articles.standfirst: El IGL de Fnatic pasó por los micrófonos de MARCA tras perder contra LOUD
articles.summary: Ayer, Fnatic cayó eliminado contra LOUD en la semifinal del VALORANT Champions en Los Ángeles. El equipo de EMEA no pudo superar a los brasileños, y finalmente el resultado fue un
articles.body: Ayer, Fnatic cayó eliminado contra LOUD en la semifinal del VALORANT Champions en Los Ángeles. El equipo de EMEA no pudo superar a los brasileños, y finalmente el resultado fue un 2-1 con el que terminan su temporada. Después del partido, MARCA pudo hablar con Boaster, el IGL del conjunto inglés sobre sus sensaciones, la temporada y el nivel de EMEA en cuanto a las principales regiones de VALORANT internacional. Pregunta: Boaster, lo siento por la derrota, ¿cómo te sientes? Respuesta: Estoy triste por la derrota, pero tuvimos un gran año, por lo que no me puedo quejar. Solo esperaba que tuvieramos una derrota mejor que la de hoy, siento que perdimos porque no jugamos como solemos hacerlo. Es igual que con DRX, pero LOUD es mucho más fuerte, y con ellos no pudimos sacarlo adelante P. ¿Qué crees que ha sido la clave que ha hecho que en este torneo no hayais podido jugar como en los dos anteriores? R. No sé. Creo que algunos de mis compañeros están cansados, quizá sin tanto hambre de ganar... Lo sentí así. Cuando ganas dos trofeos empiezas a cambiar cómo piensas en algunos momentos... no soy psicólogo, quizá necesitemos un terapeuta que nos diga qué está pasando. A pesar de la derrota, @OfficialBoaster ha hablado con nuestro compañero @mariomt13 sobre la temporada, el #VALORANTChampions y la situación de @FNATIC Muy pronto la entrevista en @marca, pero de momento os dejamos con un saludo para todos vosotros pic.twitter.com/UZJGnaBBl7? MARCA Gaming (@MarcaGaming) August 25, 2023 P. ¿Creees que la temporada es muy larga para los jugadores? R. Sí, la temporada es muy larga. He hablado con jugadores de NA y de APAC, y todos creemos que estaría bien tener un descanso un poco más largo, porque hemos terminado el año un poco tarde. Vas de un gran bloque a otro gran bloque, sobre todo para los que llegan lejos en los eventos, y siento que no tenemos tiempo de volver a recuperar nuestra creatividad. Cuando ganas un evento o quedas segundo, hay muchas emociones, adrenalina... A veces una semana no es suficiente, y cuando vuelves tienes que dar el 100%, por lo que es muy cansado. P. Hay ciertos clubes en NA que dicen que EMEA es una región de un equipo.¿Cómo crees que está el nivel de las tres regiones? R. Creo que APAC tiene DRX y Paper Rex, NA tiene algunas opciones más, porque se han combinado con Brasil, que tiene buenos equipos. Creo que nuestra región es bastante buena, en este evento teníamos a Team Liquid y NaVi en el grupo de la muerte con LOUD. Tenemos equipos muy buenos, pero nosotros, a pesar de que en los torneos anteriores fuimos capaces de sacarlo adelante, no en este caso.

articles.title: VALORANT Champions: Evil Geniuses frena la remontada de LOUD y se clasifica para la gran final
articles.standfirst: El conjunto norteamericano ha superado al brasileño y se verá las caras contra Paper Rex
articles.summary: La última semifinal del VALORANT Champions ha concluido en el KIA Forum de Los Ángeles. Evil Geniuses ha superado a LOUD en un partido muy igualado que comenzó llevándose de manera
articles.body: La última semifinal del VALORANT Champions ha concluido en el KIA Forum de Los Ángeles. Evil Geniuses ha superado a LOUD en un partido muy igualado que comenzó llevándose de manera clara en Ascent y Lotus, pero que se le ha complicado en Pearl y Split. El conjunto brasileño supo recuperarse cuando más lo necesitaba, pero no pudo cerrar la eliminatoria en un Bind en el que los de Potter han sido mejores. Se acaba así el sueño del segundo mundial consecutivo, y los genios malvados se citan mañana en la gran final contra Paper Rex. Crónica Evil Geniuses-LOUD El mapa de Ascent empezó con LOUD por delante, situándose 2-0, pero la igualdad llegó al máximo en el primer bando. Ninguno de los dos conjuntos sacó especial ventaja, pero con dos rondas increíbles, los genios alcanzaron el 5-7. El segundo bando fue favorable a Evil Geniuses, que se hacía con la ronda de pistolas y la de superioridad. Sin embargo, la bonus cayó del lado de LOUD, que no se quería rendir. Parecía que podían buscar la remontada, llegando al 8-10, pero los genios respondieron rápido, poniendo la undécima. Sin embargo, no fueron capaces de cerrar, ya que LOUD se rehízo, llevando el encuentro al overtime. En este, una triple de Jawgemo y un cierre magistral de Demon1 dieron fin al primer mapa de la semifinal. Para continuar, la elección fue Lotus. En este mapa, aunque LOUD tenía ventaja de elección, no hubo color. Evil Geniuses supo adaptarse mejor, y la defensa brasileña hizo aguas. El primer bando se inclinó claramente del lado de los genios, que lo cerraron 10-2. A pesar de que LOUD trató de remontar en su lado atacante, no pudo realmente marcar mucha diferencia. Los chicos de Potter se mostraron imparables, y consiguieron cerrar su segundo punto con un resultado de 13-4. Y cuando parecía que se acababa rápidamente la serie, LOUD ha dado con la tecla. El conjunto brasileño ha dado todo de sí, y comenzaba el Pearl muy por delante. Era un 6-0 nada más empezar, contra el que poco pudo hacer EG, y que se convirtió en un 9-3 al cambio de bando. Tras este, sin embargo, Evil Geniuses intentó darle la vuelta, apoyándose en la mejora de su ataque. Consiguió llegar hasta un resultado de 10-8, que les permitía soñar con el 3-0, pero finalmente el equipo brasileño supo cerrar y soñaba con la remontada. Split fue el cuarto mapa, y de nuevo los norteamericanos desaparecieron en defensa. LOUD, llevado en volandas por un Aspas que con Raze parecía imparable, destrozó a Evil Geniuses, y volvió a sacar una gran diferencia al cambio de lado, de 9-3. En este caso los de NA no fueron capaces de buscar la remontada con tanta fuerza, y aunque llegaron a estar 12-7, no pudieron evitar que LOUD pusiera el empate y lo llevara todo al Bind, el último mapa de la serie. La mentalidad de los estadounidenses parecía haber empeorado sobremanera, pero finalmente EG despertó cuando más lo necesitaba. Demon1 volvía a Chamber, e hizo las delicias de su equipo, que comenzaba 5-0 arriba. Finalmente, aunque LOUD se acercaba, se llevaban una ventaja de 7-5 al cambio de bando. Y estas malas sensaciones de LOUD se hicieron patentes en el lado de su ataque. No fueron capaces de sacar fuerzas de este bando, y finalmente vieron como su participación en el Champions se terminaba con un 13-8 favorable a Evil Geniuses, que se cita con Paper Rex en la final de mañana.

articles.title: Leo Faria: "El Masters de Madrid será el más competitivo porque solo irán los mejores de los mejores"
articles.standfirst: MARCA ha hablado con el director de las competiciones de VALORANT
articles.summary: El pasado miércoles Riot Games daba a conocer una gran noticia para la comunidad española de VALORANT. El primer Masters de la temporada 2023-2024 se disputará en Madrid, y en él s
articles.body: El pasado miércoles Riot Games daba a conocer una gran noticia para la comunidad española de VALORANT. El primer Masters de la temporada 2023-2024 se disputará en Madrid, y en él se citarán los ocho mejores equipos del panorama internacional. MARCA ha podido hablar con Leo Faria, Director Global de las competiciones de VALORANT sobre la decisión de elegir Madrid como ciudad para situar el torneo y la situación actual del shooter de Riot como esport a nivel mundial, tanto en las VCT como en las ligas regionales. Pregunta: Cómo crees que ha crecido el ecosistema de VALORANT. ¿Ha sido tan rápido como esperabas en todas las regiones? Respuesta: Siempre hay cosas que podemos hacer mejor. Es el primer año de la nueva estructura, es muy pronto, pero hemos visto ya buen trabajo de las tres ligas. Es justo decir que Américas es la que más se ha acercado y mejor reacción de los fans ha tenido, con más espectadores. Pero cuando miras al plano general estamos muy contentos, porque en realidad lo que importa es que la gran mayoría de la comunidad son jugadores del juego, y lo que buscamos es el número de jugadores que se acercan a ver los partidos, que ha crecido mes a mes. Nos ha costado un tiempo conseguir una audiencia, y crear un ecosistema que funcione con el formato, pero ahora mismo estamos muy felices. Es increíblemente pronto aún en el desarrollo de la escena competitiva. Si ves el crecimiento, no podemos estar más felices y tener más confianza en cómo se está haciendo. P. ¿Qué pasó con China? ¿Por qué no se la ha incluido en la liga de APAC? R. La razón principal por la que China no empezó directamente con el resto es, como sabes, que el juego no se podía jugar allí. Tienes que pedir unos permisos al gobierno, necesitas licencias, que pedimos en 2020 cuando salió VALORANT. Esa fue la razón por la que no teníamos la liga oficialmente en China. Sin embargo, la división se basa en el tamaño. Si miras la cantidad de gente en Américas, que une Norte América con América del Sur, EMEA, que es Europa, Europa del Este y África, y Pacífico, que es toda Asia menos China. El tamaño de estas regiones es más o menos como el de China sola. Una de las cosas más bonitas de VALORANT es que no hay una región que domine completamente el juego, y China es el mercado más grande del gaming en el mundo, y ese mercado tiene el potencial de tener su propia liga. A través de los clubes damos a los jugadores la oportunidad de tener una gran carrera Leo Faria P. Ha habido mucha controversia porque se han malinterpretado tus twits sobre el tier 2 de VALORANT. ¿Cuáles son los pensamientos y objetivos de Riot para esta categoría? R. Sí, fue un chiste desafortunado, porque estábamos hablando sobre qué EMEA ganaba todo y... Bueno, desafortunadamente fue interpretado de esa manera, y me arrepiento de haber hecho esas declaraciones. No miramos a ninguna de nuestras competiciones en el vacío, sino que pensamos cómo pueden ayudar a la mejora del esport. No miramos al Tier dos como si todo empezara y acabara ahí. El Tier dos, dentro de todas las capas, está enfocado a generar talento. Quieres que los que quieren ser profesionales tengan un camino claro en el que puedan concentrarse, y por el que si son suficientemente buenos, puedan llegar al Tier dos. Pero cómo hacerlo es lo complicado. Lo principal es saber que para que funcione esta parte no hay que quitarle estabilidad al nivel superior. Mucha gente pregunta por qué no tenemos más ascensos, por qué no hay descensos... dar estabilidad a los clubes de arriba es la forma de crecer. Incluso a pesar que las &apos;franquicias&apos; están basadas en los clubes, hay que tener en cuenta que es a través de esos clubes que les ofrecemos a los jugadores la oportunidad de tener una gran carrera. Las Challengers siempre estarán centradas en el desarrollo de talento, queremos asegurar que esas competiciones son suficientemente interesantes para que los clubes quieran invertir en ellas, para que los organizadores de torneos sean parte fundamental de nuestro plan. Estamos muy interesados en hacer que funcionen, pero creo que es una cuestión de hacerlo más directo, solucionar los problemas y mejorar. Una de las cosas que estamos buscando cambiar es el calendario. La temporada acabó muy pronto para los equipos que no llegaron al Ascension. En mayo ya no tenían nada que hacer. Los hemos escuchado, y haremos cambios para el año que viene. P. ¿Cómo ves ahora el camino de los jugadores desde el punto de ser buenos en el juego hasta llegar a ser profesionales? ¿Mejora con el nuevo sistema de afiliación? R. De la manera que funciona ahora mismo, si eres un buen jugador que está abajo y dices: &apos;¿Sabes qué? Podría intentar convertirme en profesional&apos;, tienes varias opciones. Para la mayoría de casos lo que sucede es que haces un equipo y lo intnetas en los clasificatorios abiertos. Aquí, cuando llegas a Challengers hay dos opciones. O tu equipo en general es lo suficientemente bueno, o tú eres suficientemente bueno y los clubes se fijan en tí y te fichan. Al final, los mejores jugadores siempre llegan a lo más alto. Esto lo hemos visto en las franquicias. Un buen ejemplo es Optic. No llegaron a franquicias, pero la mayoría de los jugadores se fueron a NRG. Hoy en día hay un camino, que en EMEA es un poco diferente, porque tenemos las VRC, que al final son el camino de la comunidad a ese segundo tier. P. Pasemos ahora a hablar del Masters de Madrid, cuál es la historia destrás. ¿Por qué Madrid y por qué el primer Masters del año? Deseábamos ir a Madrid desde hace tiempo. La comunidad, lo grande que es cómo de unida está y la pasión que tiene nos atraían mucho. El primer torneo al que fui dentro del equipo de VALORANT fue Copenhague, y allí conocí a Mixwell, que me dijo que teníamos que llevar un evento a España. Masters is coming to Madrid! https://t.co/AkZrJUjOIo? Leo Faria (@lhfaria) August 23, 2023 Ya estábamos trabajando en ello, pero eso es lo que oíamos en todos lados, la gran pasión que los aficionados españoles tenían por VALORANT, tenemos el equipo de Barcelona que nos decía lo mismo... Parecía la decisión obvia. Siempre estamos viendo los próximos lugares, teniendo en cuenta dónde hemos estado, a dónde vamos... Queríamos volver a EMEA y España parecía la mejor opción, y en una gran ciudad como Madrid, en la que ya hemos estado otras veces, como en 2019... &quot;El Masters de Madrid será el más competitivo, porque solo irán los mejores de los mejores&quot; Leo Faria P. ¿Por qué decidisteis que fuera el primer Masters del año, que a su vez es el que menos equipos tiene? ¿Por qué habéis decidido hacer este cambio, y, ha llegado para quedarse? R. Todas las veces que hacemos algo nuevo, es lo último hasta que deja de serlo. No sé si este será el formato de ahora en adelante, pero tampoco se si lo cambiaremos. Proponemos cosas, vemos cómo van, y las ajustamos. La principal razón por la que hemos implementado que solo sean ocho equipos es porque queremos que la temporada se vea como un progreso. Será el Masters más pequeño, pero también será el más competitivo, porque solo irán los mejores de los mejores. Que haya menos equipos no significa que no vaya a haber intensidad, que no vayamos a poner el mismo esfuerzo. Vamos a poner toda nuestra energía, vamos a buscar la mejor calidad de producción... Va a ser un grandísimo evento.

articles.title: Riot Games confía en Premier como vía de ascenso a las VRL en los próximos años
articles.standfirst: En España por el momento continuará siendo mediante el Circuito Tormenta
articles.summary: Este último año, Riot Games, empresa desarrolladora de los dos esports más laureados de los últimos años, el League of Legends y el VALORANT, nos presentaba Premier, el sistema de
articles.body: Este último año, Riot Games, empresa desarrolladora de los dos esports más laureados de los últimos años, el League of Legends y el VALORANT, nos presentaba Premier, el sistema de torneos interno del shooter, que llevaba el ecosistema competitivo a todos los jugadores. Ahora, han querido sacar a relucir los siguientes pasos que este modo va a dar, desde que vuelva al juego el próximo 29 de agosto, con múltiples cambios, entre los que se cuentan nuevas divisiones y distintas recompensas para los jugadores. Premier, la vía de ascenso al ecosistema profesional Este día antes mencionado comienza la &apos;Fase 1&apos;. Esta durará desde este próximo martes hasta el 22 de octubre. En esta fase el torneo contará con partidas semanales, que permitirán a los equipos conseguir una puntuación determinada. Aquellos que consigan más de 675 de puntuación de Premier se clasificarán para las eliminatorias. Cada partida que los jugadores ganen en este modo de juego les permitirá recibir recompensas, como amuletos de arma de las divisiones en las que se encuentre su equipo. Cada uno de los conjuntos será situado en una división entre Abierta, Intermedia, Avanzada, Élite y Contendiente. Uníos a Andy Ho, director de juego de VALORANT, y a Leo Faria, director internacional de los esports de VALORANT, para descubrir las interesantes novedades que llegarán a Premier durante su lanzamiento oficial y a lo largo de 2024.Ahora jugaremos en serio. ¿Os apuntáis? pic.twitter.com/OR3sTsM1oK? VALORANT (@VALORANTes) August 25, 2023 Precisamente estos últimos, los clasificados en &apos;Contendiente&apos;, podrían tener una recompensa aún mayor a partir de la próxima temporada. Según señaló Leo Faria, Director del apartado competitivo de VALORANT, su objetivo es que Premier de paso al mundo profesional: &quot;En el futuro esperamos que Premier sea el camino a seguir para ser profesionales. Queremos una línea clara a seguir para llegar a lo más alto, y queremos que empiece en el juego&quot;. Sin embargo, esto choca con la situación actual de nuestro país. En España, y en EMEA en general, el ascenso a la VRL, la Rising se da desde el Circuito Tormenta, las VRC. Por el momento, estas competiciones se van a mantener, lo que haría que Premier no diera ascenso, al menos aún, a la Rising en nuestro país.

Queremos una línea clara a seguir para llegar a lo más alto, y queremos que empiece en el juego&quot;. Sin embargo, esto choca con la situación actual de nuestro país. En España, y en EMEA en general, el ascenso a la VRL, la Rising se da desde el Circuito Tormenta, las VRC. Por el momento, estas competiciones se van a mantener, lo que haría que Premier no diera ascenso, al menos aún, a la Rising en nuestro país.

articles.title: Evil Geniuses se resarce, y se convierte en campeón mundial contra Paper Rex
articles.standfirst: Se han impuesto 3-1 al equipo de APAC y son los terceros campeones de la historia
articles.summary: Se acabó el VALORANT Champions. El torneo más importante del shooter de Riot Games llega a su fin tras una temporada muy larga, en la que Evil Geniuses, el equipo norteamericano se
articles.body: Se acabó el VALORANT Champions. El torneo más importante del shooter de Riot Games llega a su fin tras una temporada muy larga, en la que Evil Geniuses, el equipo norteamericano se ha proclamado campeón, tras ganar a Paper Rex en la Gran Final. El equipo dirigido por Potter ha superado los múltiples problemas y se ha convertido en el campeón del mundo cuando casi nadie se lo esperaba. Y además lo ha hecho recuperándose y vengándose de los de APAC en una final que ha terminado 3-1 a su favor. Evil Geniuses es el tercer campeón del mundo de VALORANT El primer mapa fue split. Todo el encuentro se vio muy marcado por una constante: Paper Rex destacaba en ataque, pero se complicaba mucho las cosas en defensa. Evil Geniuses sacó las dos primeras rondas, pero no pudo evitar que los de APAC acabaran su apartado ofensivo con un resultado a favor de 8-4. Sin embargo, como decimos, los problemas llegaron para los de Alecks cuando tuvieron que defender. Su estilo, tan ofensivo y poco ordenado fue superado con claridad por los de Potter. Comenzaron una remontada que pronto llegó al 8-8, y finalmente el resultado alcanzó el 10-13, siendo el primer punto para los de NA. En Ascent parecía que la dinámica podía ser la misma. Paper Rex empezó en ataque, y lo hizo con un 4-0. Evil Geniuses, sin embargo, supo responder ahora, e igualó ligeramente el partido para el cambio de bando, situando un 7-5 a la mitad. Y de nuevo, cuando tocó defender, Paper Rex tuvo problemas. EG se recuperó, y cuando quisieron darse cuenta los de Alecks, el marcador era un 7-9. Sin embargo, en esta ocasión los asiáticos fueron capaces de darle la vuelta, cerrando con un ajustado resultado de 13-11, que ponía el 1-1 global. Bind era el tercer mapa, el del primer desempate. En él, de nuevo Paper Rex empezaba atacando, pero en este caso los genios no dieron opción en el primer bando. Paper Rex empezaba con mal pie, y el resultado llegó a reflejar un 1-7 para los americanos. Parecía que podían responder los asiáticos, pero finalmente, al cambio de bando el marcador era 3-9. Y tras la media parte, como era de esperar, las opciones de Paper Rex no parecían mejorar. Por mucho que ganaron la ronda de pistolas y la de superioridad, no fueron capaces de llevarlo más allá. Evil Geniuses superó claramente a sus rivales, y el resultado final del mapa fue un 5-13. Lotus podía ser el último escenario, uno en el que Evil Geniuses no habia perdido en todo lo que llevábamos de torneo. Sin embargo, Paper Rex no dudó a la hora de atacar, y comenzaba con dos rondas de altísimo nivel. Aun así, EG contestaba, y al cambio de bando la diferencia solo llegó a un 5-7. En la segunda mitad, la ronda de pistolas fue para EG, y también la de superioridad. Paper Rex volvió a pagar sus problemas en defensa, y veía cómo los genios se ponían 9-7. Sin embargo, alcanzaron de nuevo las tablas, llegando al 9-9. Sin embargo, hasta aquí llegó la posibilidad de Paper Rex. EG consiguió sacar ventaja con mucho acierto de Jawgemo and Boostio, y cerró el encuentro con un resultado final de 13-10.

articles.title: Riot Games presenta el nuevo mapa de VALORANT: Sunset
articles.standfirst: La desarrolladora lo mostró al público en la final del mundial
articles.summary: Riot Games llevaba un tiempo mencionando que tenían algo especial para enseñar a sus fans en la final del mundial. Más allá del propio partido, en el que los espectadores disfrutar
articles.body: Riot Games llevaba un tiempo mencionando que tenían algo especial para enseñar a sus fans en la final del mundial. Más allá del propio partido, en el que los espectadores disfrutaron del VALORANT del más alto nivel, ahora han dado a conocer el nuevo mapa. Sunset es la nueva localización que llega al juego en el acto II del episodio siete. Está basado en la ciudad en la que se encuentra la oficina central de Riot Games, Los Ángeles, y está repleto de distintos detalles que recuerdan a la ciudad estadounidense. Estas son algunas de las claves de Sunset. Así es Sunset, el nuevo mapa de VALORANT Hoy 29 de agosto de 2023, los fans de VALORANT podrán disfrutar en sus casas del siguiente paso del juego desarrollado por Riot Games. El shooter llega al episodio dos del séptimo acto, y lo hace con este nuevo mapa. Con dos zonas para plantar la bomba, Sunset es un mapa clásico, con tres carriles. El tercero, el del medio será fundamental para que los jugadores puedan vencer, ya que tomar el control de este punto es clave en este escenario. Como ya hemos señalado, el mapa tiene como referencia la ciudad de Los Ángeles. Es por eso que, según señala Joe Lansford, uno de los puntos de más complicación fue la iluminación: &quot;Lo más complicado fue encontrar el punto perfecto para la luz; hubo mucho trabajo y colaboración de arte y diseño. Queríamos encapsular ese rollo del atardecer de Los Ángeles con un cielo rosado y sombras altas, pero iba a impactar negativamente la experiencia de juego&quot;. Y finalmente, Riot Games ha presentado un mapa sencillo, con aire clásico de shooter, pero lleno de easter eggs que los jugadores podrán tratar de encontrar. Sin embargo, desde un primer momento no pensaban en que fuera tan clásico, tal y como indica Lansford: &quot;En una versión inicial de Sunset, había piscinas de ácido que hacían daño si entrabas&quot;.

articles.title: Ben Affleck se desvela como fan de VALORANT en la final del Champions de Los Ángeles
articles.standfirst: El actor demostró conocimiento del juego de Riot Games
articles.summary: El pasado sábado Riot Games llevó a Los Ángeles la gran fiesta del VALORANT. El mundial del shooter táctico tuvo su gran final entre Evil Geniuses y Paper Rex. Finalmente el conjun
articles.body: El pasado sábado Riot Games llevó a Los Ángeles la gran fiesta del VALORANT. El mundial del shooter táctico tuvo su gran final entre Evil Geniuses y Paper Rex. Finalmente el conjunto de los norteamericanos fue el que se hizo con la victoria en el torneo, proclamándose los terceros campeones de la historia. En dicha final no faltaron algunas caras conocidas. Más allá de los streamers y fans del VALORANT, hubo dos personalidades que no se quisieron perder el espectáculo de Los Ángeles. Elon Musk fue con sus hijos, y también estuvo por allí Ben Affleck, que demostró su conocimiento del juego. &quot;Soy un poco promiscuo con los agentes que maineo&quot; El actor estuvo en la zona VIP antes de la gran final. En ella se encontraban muchas de las grandes personalidades, al nivel del gran evento que se vivía en el KIA Forum de Los Ángeles. Affleck, que se encontraba con sus hijos, no dudó sin embargo en demostrar que él también es un fan del VALORANT. &quot;Ahora mismo maineo Kay/o. Raze es el otro agente que juego más. Soy un poco promiscuo con los agentes que utilizo, me gusta variar&quot;, indicaba. Así explicaba Affleck los personajes del juego con los que más le gusta disputar las partidas.
